changelog: The Real-Time Power chart now loads today's Battery, AC, Solar and Output history in every time zone, including the US, where it used to fail and stay empty. It keeps updating every minute while the screen is open, starts a new day at midnight, and shows a gap where the device sent no reading or was off instead of a 0 W dip or a straight line across the missing hours. Each device's chart now shows only that device's data, and signing out clears the saved history, so switching devices or accounts no longer shows another device's or a previous session's readings. Continue as Guest has been removed from the sign-in screen.

Adding a device no longer reports The device disconnected during setup after the Wi-Fi details were accepted. Once the device has taken the Wi-Fi details it leaves Bluetooth to join Wi-Fi, and the app now treats that as the expected hand-off instead of a failed setup while you name the device or it is being added to your account.

The Add Device search screen no longer jumps when it opens or a few seconds later. It opens straight on the search with the radar already moving, instead of flashing a Checking Bluetooth overlay or the previous attempt's No Devices Found message. Allowing the Bluetooth permission, or closing any other system prompt, no longer restarts the search and empties the list of devices already found.

The app no longer shows a long black screen when it opens or comes back while Google's font service is slow or unreachable. The SIERRO start screen appears at once, and the app finishes loading in the system font if the web fonts never arrive.

Insights now reports energy in Wh. Week is a line chart you can tap to read each day. Input is split into Solar and AC, and AC charging now counts toward input. Days with no records show as gaps instead of 0, and long periods such as a month no longer drop their later days.
Opening the app with no devices goes straight to the empty Device page instead of briefly showing three placeholder device cards first.
The Insights page header is now exactly the same height as the Device page header when you have no devices, so the page titles no longer shift when switching tabs.

The switch on each device card is now labelled AC Output, and a charging device shows Charging under its battery level, so switching the AC outlets off is no longer mistaken for turning the whole unit off.
The QR scanner's camera view no longer shows a large stretched play button while the camera permission is being asked for, while the camera starts, or when the scanner closes.

If Bluetooth drops while the Wi-Fi details are being sent during setup, the app now reconnects on its own up to three times, showing Reconnecting to device (1/3), and resends the Wi-Fi details without asking for the password again. The Device disconnected screen only appears if every attempt fails.

When a device has no readings (for example it is powered off), its page shows -- for AC, Solar and Output instead of 0 W, and no runtime estimate, so a missing reading no longer looks like zero power.

With no internet connection (Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and mobile data all off), the Device list and device page now say so instead of showing Connected, and the AC switch is locked until the network is back. The device itself is not marked offline, and its state is read again as soon as the connection returns.
Fan Speed is no longer shown in Device Settings. It remains available in internal QA builds only while it is verified on hardware.

On the verification code screen the cursor now moves to the box the next digit goes into, instead of staying in the first box while you type. Tapping a box no longer lets a digit be inserted in the middle of the code.

The AC switch on each device card now shows what the device reports. It no longer turns itself back on a few minutes after being switched off, a switch made on another phone shows up when you return to the app, and an offline or powered-off device shows its switch off. After switching, the app checks with the device and says so if the outlets did not change.

The notification bell and the Notifications list now cover the same alerts from all your devices. An alert on a device other than the one last opened is listed with that device's name, opening the list clears the bell, and a list that could not load says so with Retry instead of "You're all caught up".

Device Settings has a Fan Speed slider (0–100 %). Letting go of the slider sets the fan speed on the device; if the device refuses, the slider returns to the last speed it accepted. It is unavailable while the device is offline.

Error messages shown to users no longer contain raw exception text. IllegalArgument, exception class names, stack traces, JVM package paths and unmapped backend strings are replaced with the existing reviewed message for that screen, or a generic one. The full text is still written to the console for diagnosis.

Smart Schedule is paused. Its settings entry is no longer shown, no new charge-window writes are made for it on the device or in the background, and a schedule saved while a device was offline is kept rather than sent. Sleep Mode, including its background timer, is unaffected.

Dedicated AWS Sleep Mode timer applies charge power through passthrough while the app is closed. Saves verify account/device ownership; scheduled writes support timezone-aware windows, retry, deduplication and serialized cancellation.

Removed the background-save warning toast after Sleep Mode or Smart Schedule settings are accepted by the device. Unconfirmed background stops and device-write failures still show their existing messages.

PV, solar, photovoltaic and MPPT alarms are hidden from Notifications, unread badges and foreground alarm pushes. Normal solar-charging status notifications and unrelated device alarms remain available; the relay no longer mistakes PV power failures for grid outages.

Stopping an absent background schedule no longer requires a poller session. Relay failures retain the Sleep Mode editor for retry and explain missing-session or network errors; device settings no longer display the global Smart Schedule preference as this device's status.

Sleep Mode and Smart Schedule now recognize additional explicit missing-config error spellings, including not exists and the reported config contribute wording, without bypassing power-write, permission or network failures.
Offline Smart Schedule saves are queued per account and device, with guarded replay and visible pending or background-failure feedback.
Bluetooth setup now serializes connections and commands, respects small MTUs, cancels disconnected operations, supports open Wi-Fi and avoids replaying device creation requests.
Schedule saves only bypass explicitly missing sleepMode attributes; cached capability results no longer hide permission or network failures.

Power outage alerts now go only to the accounts a device is actually bound to. A push registration without a signed-in account is refused, and signing in on a device moves its push token off whichever account held it before, so an outage on someone else's battery can no longer reach you.

AC, solar and output power now read as unavailable instead of a nonsense figure such as 65534 W when the device has no reading for that channel, and the battery ring no longer turns one into a time estimate like "0h1m remaining". Battery power is left out too whenever one of those channels is missing, rather than being computed from a placeholder.
